/-!
# Cereceda's conjecture

Cereceda's conjecture concerns the diameter of the space of $(d + 2)$-colourings of a
$d$-degenerate graph, where two proper colourings are adjacent when they differ on exactly one
vertex. It states that this diameter is $O(n^2)$ for graphs on $n$ vertices.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Cereceda's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cereceda%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Graph_theory)
- [BH19] Bousquet, N., Heinrich, M., *A polynomial version of Cereceda's conjecture*,
  [arXiv:1903.05619](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.05619)
- [EF18] Eiben, E., Feghali, C., *Towards Cereceda's conjecture for planar graphs*,
  [arXiv:1810.00731](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.00731)
- [Ce07] Cereceda, L., *Mixing graph colourings*, PhD thesis, London School of Economics (2007),
  [http://etheses.lse.ac.uk/131/](http://etheses.lse.ac.uk/131/)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A graph `G` is `d`-degenerate if every nonempty subgraph of `G` has a vertex of degree at
most `d`. Equivalently, every nonempty set `S` of vertices contains a vertex with at most `d`
neighbours in `S`. The degeneracy of `G` is the least `d` for which `G` is `d`-degenerate, so
`IsDegenerate G d` says exactly that the degeneracy of `G` is at most `d`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: SimpleGraph.minDegree / SimpleGraph.induce (would need quantification over induced subgraphs with Fintype instances); SimpleGraph.Subgraph; no degeneracy or colouring-number definition exists in Mathlib (rg 'degener' in Mathlib/Combinatorics finds nothing relevant).
justification.name: CerecedasConjecture.IsDegenerate
justification.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no notion of graph degeneracy / d-degenerate graphs. Defined as: every nonempty set S of vertices contains a vertex with at most d neighbours in S (encard-based, so also meaningful for infinite graphs); this is 'every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree ≤ d', i.e. degeneracy ≤ d. Tested: ⊥ is 0-degenerate, K_{n+2} is not n-degenerate, monotone in d.

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem recoloringGraph_bot_fin_one (k : ℕ) :
    recoloringGraph (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 1)) k = ⊤ := by
  ext α β
  simp only [recoloringGraph_adj, top_adj]
  refine ⟨fun ⟨_, hv, _⟩ h => hv (h ▸ rfl), fun h => ⟨0, fun h0 => h ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · exact RelHom.ext fun w => Subsingleton.elim w 0 ▸ h0
  · exact fun w hw => absurd (Subsingleton.elim w 0) hw

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isDegenerate_top_fin (d : ℕ) : IsDegenerate (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (d + 1))) d := by
  intro S hS
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hS
  refine ⟨v, hv, ?_⟩
  have h1 : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (d + 1))).neighborSet v ∩ S ⊆ Set.univ \ {v} := by
    intro w hw
    simp only [Set.mem_inter_iff, mem_neighborSet, top_adj] at hw
    exact ⟨Set.mem_univ _, fun h => hw.1 (Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp h).symm⟩
  calc _ ≤ (Set.univ \ {v} : Set (Fin (d + 1))).encard := Set.encard_le_encard h1
    _ = d := by
        rw [Set.encard_diff_singleton_of_mem (Set.mem_univ v), Set.encard_univ,
          ENat.card_eq_coe_fintype_card, Fintype.card_fin]
        norm_cast

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isDegenerate_top (n : ℕ) : ¬ IsDegenerate (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (n + 2))) n := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨v, -, hv⟩ := h Set.univ Set.univ_nonempty
  have : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (n + 2))).neighborSet v = Set.univ \ {v} := by ext; simp [eq_comm]

    ENat.card_eq_coe_fintype_card, Fintype.card_fin] at hv
  norm_num at hv

@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem cerecedas_conjecture (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), IsDegenerate G d →
      (recoloringGraph G (d + 2)).ediam ≤ C * Fintype.card V ^ 2 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Cereceda's conjecture** (Cereceda, 2007; see [BH19], Conjecture 3).

For every $d$ there is a constant $C_d$ such that for every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with
degeneracy at most $d$ (every nonempty subgraph of $G$ has a vertex of degree at most $d$), the
diameter of the space of proper $(d + 2)$-colourings of $G$ is at most $C_d \cdot n^2$. Here two
colourings are adjacent if they differ on exactly one vertex, so this says that any two proper
$(d + 2)$-colourings of $G$ can be transformed into each other by a sequence of at most
$C_d \cdot n^2$ single-vertex recolourings through proper $(d + 2)$-colourings. In other words,
the diameter of the space of $(d + 2)$-colourings of $d$-degenerate graphs is $O(n^2)$.

Since `SimpleGraph.ediam` takes the value `⊤` on a disconnected graph with at least two
vertices, the bound also asserts that the recolouring graph is connected. The constant $C_d$ is
allowed to depend on $d$, following [BH19], where the version with a constant independent of $d$
is stated separately as a stronger question.

  sorry

claims.decomposer_note: Single Prop: for every d ≥ 1 there is a constant C_d such that for every graph G on n vertices with degeneracy ≤ d (every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree ≤ d), any two proper (d+2)-colorings of G are joined by a sequence of at most C_d·n² single-vertex recolorings through proper (d+2)-colorings (the recoloring graph is connected with diameter ≤ C_d n²); the constant is allowed to depend on d following Bousquet–Heinrich, who explicitly state the d-uniform-constant version only as a separate stronger 'Question', and allowing k ≥ d+2 colors instead of exactly d+2 is equivalent for fixed d.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful content (∀ d, ∃ C_d, every finite d-degenerate graph has (d+2)-recolouring-graph diameter ≤ C_d·n², adjacency = differ on exactly one vertex, connectivity forced via ediam=⊤ or explicit walks); the encodings (ediam vs. Walk vs. Fin (m+1)-sequence; Fin n vs. Fintype V; with/without 1 ≤ d) are all equivalent. c07 was chosen as the base: it uses Mathlib's SimpleGraph.ediam (the most direct reading of 'diameter of the space of colourings'), an encard-based degeneracy definition that is correct on all inputs, quantifies over all d as in Bousquet–Heinrich's Conjecture and the Wikipedia span, and has the best API/test coverage. Edits: replaced c07's fromRel adjacency with c08's transparent structural definition (∃ v, α v ≠ β v ∧ ∀ w ≠ v, α w = β w), adapted the one-vertex test accordingly, added c03's positive test that K_{d+1} is d-degenerate, cited EF18, and wrapped an over-long URL line.
claims.source_text: for graphs with degeneracy at most d, and for (d + 2)-colorings of these graphs, the diameter of the space of colorings is O(n2)
claims.text_span: for graphs with degeneracy at most d, and for (d + 2)-colorings of these graphs, the diameter of the space of colorings is O(n2)

context: In the mathematics of graph coloring, Cereceda’s conjecture is an unsolved problem on the distance between pairs of colorings of sparse graphs. It states that, for two different colorings of a graph of degeneracy d, both using at most d + 2 colors, it should be possible to reconfigure one coloring into the other by changing the color of one vertex at a time, using a number of steps that is quadratic in the size of the graph. The conjecture is named after Luis Cereceda, who formulated it in his 2007 doctoral dissertation.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the source; the only nit is that the notes' 'd ≥ 1' restriction is not in Wikipedia or Bousquet–Heinrich, so the file quantifies over all d (mathematically equivalent since the d = 0 case is trivial).

/-!
# Cereceda's conjecture

Cereceda's conjecture concerns the diameter of the space of $(d + 2)$-colourings of a
$d$-degenerate graph, where two proper colourings are adjacent when they differ on exactly one
vertex. It states that this diameter is $O(n^2)$ for graphs on $n$ vertices.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Cereceda's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cereceda%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Graph_theory)
- [BH19] Bousquet, N., Heinrich, M., *A polynomial version of Cereceda's conjecture*,
  [arXiv:1903.05619](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.05619)
- [EF18] Eiben, E., Feghali, C., *Towards Cereceda's conjecture for planar graphs*,
  [arXiv:1810.00731](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.00731)
- [Ce07] Cereceda, L., *Mixing graph colourings*, PhD thesis, London School of Economics (2007),
  [http://etheses.lse.ac.uk/131/](http://etheses.lse.ac.uk/131/)
-/

namespace CerecedasConjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)

/--
A graph `G` is `d`-degenerate if every nonempty subgraph of `G` has a vertex of degree at
most `d`. Equivalently, every nonempty set `S` of vertices contains a vertex with at most `d`
neighbours in `S`. The degeneracy of `G` is the least `d` for which `G` is `d`-degenerate, so
`IsDegenerate G d` says exactly that the degeneracy of `G` is at most `d`.
-/
def IsDegenerate (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set V, S.Nonempty → ∃ v ∈ S, (G.neighborSet v ∩ S).encard ≤ d

/--
The `k`-recolouring graph (also called the `k`-reconfiguration graph) of `G`: its vertices are
the proper `k`-colourings of `G`, and two colourings are adjacent when they differ on exactly
one vertex, i.e. when one is obtained from the other by recolouring a single vertex.
-/
def recoloringGraph (k : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (G.Coloring (Fin k)) where
  Adj α β := ∃ v, α v ≠ β v ∧ ∀ w, w ≠ v → α w = β w
  symm _ _ := fun ⟨v, hv, h⟩ => ⟨v, hv.symm, fun w hw => (h w hw).symm⟩
  loopless _ := fun ⟨_, hv, _⟩ => hv rfl

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem recoloringGraph_adj (k : ℕ) (α β : G.Coloring (Fin k)) :
    (recoloringGraph G k).Adj α β ↔ ∃ v, α v ≠ β v ∧ ∀ w, w ≠ v → α w = β w :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- On a one-vertex graph, any two distinct colourings are adjacent in the recolouring graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem recoloringGraph_bot_fin_one (k : ℕ) :
    recoloringGraph (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 1)) k = ⊤ := by
  ext α β
  simp only [recoloringGraph_adj, top_adj]
  refine ⟨fun ⟨_, hv, _⟩ h => hv (h ▸ rfl), fun h => ⟨0, fun h0 => h ?_, ?_⟩⟩
  · exact RelHom.ext fun w => Subsingleton.elim w 0 ▸ h0
  · exact fun w hw => absurd (Subsingleton.elim w 0) hw

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsDegenerate.mono {d d' : ℕ} (h : d ≤ d') (hG : IsDegenerate G d) : IsDegenerate G d' :=
  fun S hS => (hG S hS).imp fun v ⟨hv, hd⟩ => ⟨hv, hd.trans (by exact_mod_cast h)⟩

/-- The edgeless graph is `0`-degenerate. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isDegenerate_bot : IsDegenerate (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) 0 := by
  refine fun S hS => hS.imp fun v hv => ⟨hv, ?_⟩
  have : (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).neighborSet v = ∅ := by ext; simp
  simp [this]

/-- The complete graph on `d + 1` vertices is `d`-degenerate. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isDegenerate_top_fin (d : ℕ) : IsDegenerate (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (d + 1))) d := by
  intro S hS
  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hS
  refine ⟨v, hv, ?_⟩
  have h1 : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (d + 1))).neighborSet v ∩ S ⊆ Set.univ \ {v} := by
    intro w hw
    simp only [Set.mem_inter_iff, mem_neighborSet, top_adj] at hw
    exact ⟨Set.mem_univ _, fun h => hw.1 (Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp h).symm⟩
  calc _ ≤ (Set.univ \ {v} : Set (Fin (d + 1))).encard := Set.encard_le_encard h1
    _ = d := by
        rw [Set.encard_diff_singleton_of_mem (Set.mem_univ v), Set.encard_univ,
          ENat.card_eq_coe_fintype_card, Fintype.card_fin]
        norm_cast

/-- The complete graph on `n + 2` vertices is not `n`-degenerate. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isDegenerate_top (n : ℕ) : ¬ IsDegenerate (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (n + 2))) n := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨v, -, hv⟩ := h Set.univ Set.univ_nonempty
  have : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (n + 2))).neighborSet v = Set.univ \ {v} := by ext; simp [eq_comm]
  rw [Set.inter_univ, this, Set.encard_diff_singleton_of_mem (Set.mem_univ v), Set.encard_univ,
    ENat.card_eq_coe_fintype_card, Fintype.card_fin] at hv
  norm_num at hv

/--
**Cereceda's conjecture** (Cereceda, 2007; see [BH19], Conjecture 3).

For every $d$ there is a constant $C_d$ such that for every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with
degeneracy at most $d$ (every nonempty subgraph of $G$ has a vertex of degree at most $d$), the
diameter of the space of proper $(d + 2)$-colourings of $G$ is at most $C_d \cdot n^2$. Here two
colourings are adjacent if they differ on exactly one vertex, so this says that any two proper
$(d + 2)$-colourings of $G$ can be transformed into each other by a sequence of at most
$C_d \cdot n^2$ single-vertex recolourings through proper $(d + 2)$-colourings. In other words,
the diameter of the space of $(d + 2)$-colourings of $d$-degenerate graphs is $O(n^2)$.

Since `SimpleGraph.ediam` takes the value `⊤` on a disconnected graph with at least two
vertices, the bound also asserts that the recolouring graph is connected. The constant $C_d$ is
allowed to depend on $d$, following [BH19], where the version with a constant independent of $d$
is stated separately as a stronger question.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem cerecedas_conjecture (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), IsDegenerate G d →
      (recoloringGraph G (d + 2)).ediam ≤ C * Fintype.card V ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end CerecedasConjecture

items: The terse list entry was expanded using the Wikipedia article's 'Statement' section and Bousquet–Heinrich (arXiv:1903.05619, Conjecture 3): for every d there is C_d such that every d-degenerate graph on n vertices has (d+2)-recolouring diameter ≤ C_d·n². The constant is allowed to depend on d, per the decomposition notes (the d-uniform version is only a separate 'Question' in BH19).

d ranges over all ℕ (no `1 ≤ d` hypothesis), following both Wikipedia ('degeneracy at most d') and BH19 ('for every d'). The d = 0 case (edgeless graphs, 2 colours) is trivially true with C = 1, so this is equivalent to the table's 'for every d ≥ 1' phrasing.
Exactly d + 2 colours are used (`G.Coloring (Fin (d + 2))`), matching Wikipedia and the slot text, rather than BH19's 'k ≥ d+2' phrasing (equivalent for fixed d, as the table notes).
The constant C is a natural number. Since the diameter is integer-valued, a real constant can be replaced by its ceiling, so this is equivalent to allowing a real C_d.

Degeneracy ≤ d is formalised via induced subgraphs only ('every nonempty vertex set S has a vertex with ≤ d neighbours inside S'); this is equivalent to the 'every nonempty subgraph' definition since a subgraph's degrees are bounded by those of the induced subgraph on the same vertex set.

Diameter is expressed with `SimpleGraph.ediam : ℕ∞`. On a disconnected recolouring graph with at least two colourings ediam = ⊤, so `ediam ≤ C * n^2` also asserts connectivity of the recolouring graph (as the conjecture intends). Boundary: if V is empty there is exactly one colouring and ediam = 0 ≤ 0; d-degenerate graphs always admit (d+2)-colourings, so the hypothesis is never vacuous.

Graphs are taken on an arbitrary finite vertex type `V : Type` (universe 0, as in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SidorenkoConjecture.lean) with n = Fintype.card V; this loses nothing since every finite graph is isomorphic to one on Fin n.

Adjacency in the recolouring graph is 'differ on exactly one vertex' (α ≠ β ∧ ∃ v, ∀ w ≠ v, α w = β w), i.e. a single-vertex recolouring between proper colourings — Glauber moves, not Kempe-chain moves.

Bespoke definitions were kept in the problem file (rather than FormalConjecturesForMathlib) because the task restricts writing to the single candidate file; they are namespaced under CerecedasConjecture and used with application syntax.

reviewer_notes: Source check: Bousquet–Heinrich (arXiv:1903.05619) state the conjecture as 'For every d, there exists C_d such that for every d-degenerate graph G, the diameter of G(G,k) is at most C_d·n² as long as k ≥ d+2', with the d-uniform constant only as a separate 'Question'; Eiben–Feghali state it with 'd a positive integer' and exactly d+2 colours. The final file uses exactly d+2 colours (Fin (d+2) palette, colours need not all be used — the standard meaning of a k-colouring) and a d-dependent constant C : ℕ (equivalent to a real constant by ceiling since the diameter is integer-valued). The table's 'd ≥ 1' hypothesis was not included: neither Wikipedia nor BH19 has it, and the d = 0 case (edgeless graphs, hypercube recolouring graph of diameter n) is trivially true, so the two readings are logically equivalent. Boundary cases: empty vertex type gives ediam = 0 ≤ 0; a d-degenerate finite graph always has a (d+2)-colouring so the colouring type is never empty; disconnected recolouring graphs give ediam = ⊤ so the bound also asserts connectivity (a known theorem), matching the literature's convention that the k-recolouring diameter is +∞ when disconnected. ediam ≤ k for finite k is equivalent to 'every pair of colourings is joined by a walk of length ≤ k', so the explicit-walk encodings of c02/c04/c05/c06 are equivalent to the shipped statement; they were not preferred only for readability/API reasons. No candidate omitted the slot and no candidate had a faithfulness defect; the bespoke definitions (IsDegenerate, recoloringGraph) are kept in the problem file with API/test lemmas, since Mathlib has neither degeneracy nor recolouring graphs. File compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
